query_normalized: analyzing the trade‑off between prompt size and code generation quality computer science
rationale: The paper focuses on model compression and deployment efficiency (quantization bit-widths) rather than the relationship between prompt size (input token length) and code generation quality. While both involve "size," the paper addresses the size of the *model parameters* to reduce cost, whereas the user's question concerns the size of the *input prompt* and its effect on output quality, representing a distinct construct and mechanism.
